# Feature 3: soft delete for comments

Deleting a comment marks it deleted and keeps the row. Deleted comments do not appear in comment lists. Other behavior is unchanged.

## Rules used (Builder reads the values from the sources)
- Comment delete behavior: app/src/app/routes/article/article.service.ts, deleteComment.
- Comment list filter: article.service.ts, getCommentsByArticle.
- Comment model fields: app/src/prisma/schema.prisma, model Comment. comment.model.ts lists fewer fields. Followed schema.prisma because it defines the table.
- Error body shape: app/src/main.ts error handler, and app/src/app/models/http-exception.model.ts. The repo has no single shape. article.service.ts uses {errors: {field: [msg]}}, {message}, and {}. Followed the {errors} pattern.
- Error status codes: article.service.ts (422, 403, 404) and main.ts (401). Reuse them for the same cases.
- Migrations: app/src/prisma/migrations/, applied as described in app/README.md.

## Plan
1. Add a nullable timestamp field to Comment, with a migration.
2. deleteComment sets the field instead of removing the row.
3. getCommentsByArticle excludes marked rows, in addition to its existing filter.
4. deleteComment and updateComment exclude marked rows from lookup, so a deleted comment returns 404 (my choice).
5. Add service tests in app/src/tests/services/article.service.test.ts.

datasource db {
  provider = "postgresql"
  url      = env("DATABASE_URL")
}

generator client {
  provider        = "prisma-client-js"
  previewFeatures = []
}

model Article {
  id          Int       @id @default(autoincrement())
  slug        String    @unique
  title       String
  description String
  body        String
  createdAt   DateTime  @default(now())
  updatedAt   DateTime  @default(now())
  tagList     Tag[]
  author      User      @relation("UserArticles", fields: [authorId], onDelete: Cascade, references: [id])
  authorId    Int
  favoritedBy User[]    @relation("UserFavorites")
  comments    Comment[]
}

model Comment {
  id        Int      @id @default(autoincrement())
  createdAt DateTime @default(now())
  updatedAt DateTime @default(now())
  body      String
  article   Article  @relation(fields: [articleId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  articleId Int
  author    User     @relation(fields: [authorId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  authorId  Int
}

model Tag {
  id       Int       @id @default(autoincrement())
  name     String    @unique
  articles Article[]
}

model User {
  id         Int       @id @default(autoincrement())
  email      String    @unique
  username   String    @unique
  password   String
  image      String?   @default("https://api.realworld.io/images/smiley-cyrus.jpeg")
  bio        String?
  articles   Article[] @relation("UserArticles")
  favorites  Article[] @relation("UserFavorites")
  followedBy User[]    @relation("UserFollows")
  following  User[]    @relation("UserFollows")
  comments   Comment[]
  demo       Boolean   @default(false)
}

Feature 3 is built, but I have not run the tests or the migration. Neither can run in this session. Before the tests will pass, run `npx prisma generate` and `npx prisma migrate deploy` in `app/`.

## Answers to the two questions

1. **What happens on delete, and which comments show in lists.** Before this change, `deleteComment` removed the row with `prisma.comment.delete`. `getCommentsByArticle` returned comments whose author is the demo user or the viewer. It had no deleted-row filter, because none existed.
2. **Error response shape and status codes.** The repo does not have one shape. `main.ts` sends `err.message` as the body, and that body is whatever object the service passed in. The shapes in use are `{ errors: { field: [msg] } }` (most 422s and the auth 403), `{ message: '...' }` (403s in the article delete and update paths), and `{}` (404s in the article and comment paths). The 401 in `main.ts` uses `{ status, message }`. Status codes in use: 201, 200, 204, 401, 403, 404, 422, 500. `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` is named in the README but is not in the repo, so I could not check an upstream error shape. I added no new error paths, so the shape question did not change any code.

## Changes

- `app/src/prisma/schema.prisma`: added `deletedAt DateTime?` to `Comment`.
- `app/src/prisma/migrations/20261030120000_comment_soft_delete/migration.sql`: `ALTER TABLE "Comment" ADD COLUMN "deletedAt" TIMESTAMP(3);`
- `article.service.ts`:
  - `deleteComment` looks up only rows where `deletedAt` is null, then sets `deletedAt` to now instead of deleting.
  - `getCommentsByArticle` adds `deletedAt: null` to its existing filter.
  - `updateComment` (from the uncommitted feature 1 work) also skips marked rows, as the spec's plan item 4 asks.
- `article.service.test.ts`: added tests for the mark-not-delete path, the `deletedAt: null` lookup, the 404 on an already-deleted comment, the list filter, the list output with the following flag, and the `updateComment` lookup filter.

The working tree already had uncommitted feature 1 edits in these files. I edited around them and did not commit anything.

## Rules applied

| Rule | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Delete behavior | Mark the row with `deletedAt`, keep the row | Spec; `article.service.ts` `deleteComment` (previously hard delete) |
| List filter | `deletedAt: null`, plus the existing demo-or-viewer author filter | Spec; `article.service.ts` `getCommentsByArticle` |
| Comment fields | `deletedAt` is a nullable `TIMESTAMP(3)` | `schema.prisma` `model Comment`; `TIMESTAMP(3)` from the initial migration. The name `deletedAt` and nullability are my choice. |
| Migration folder name | `YYYYMMDDHHMMSS_name` | Existing folders in `app/src/prisma/migrations/`. The timestamp is my choice. |
| Not-found status and body | 404 with `{}` | `article.service.ts` `deleteComment` and `updateComment`, existing code |
| Error body shape | Not used; no new error paths | Section 2 above |
| Delete of another user's comment | Still 404, not 403 | `deleteComment` lookup filters by author, so the 403 branch cannot be reached. I left it unchanged. |

## Choices and gaps

- A deleted comment returns 404 on PUT and DELETE. This is the spec's own choice (plan item 4).
- The new tests check the Prisma call arguments, because the mock returns whatever it is given. The list test shows the filter is sent to Prisma, but it does not prove the database hides deleted rows.
- Not run: the tests, `prisma generate`, and the migration. Until `prisma generate` runs, the new `deletedAt` field will not type-check.
